findings.title: Parse fast flag in any position
findings.text: The flag is only recognized as `$1`, so `scripts/check.sh baseline --fast` falls through to the `baseline [file]` handling and treats `--fast` as a filename instead of the documented usage error (exit 2); `plan --fast` is also rejected. Extract `--fast` from any position before parsing the step, then let the existing step validation reject it beside `baseline`/`decision`.
findings.existing_code:
fast=0
if [ "${1:-}" = "--fast" ]; then
  fast=1
  shift
fi

findings.title: Report missing tooling in fast mode
findings.text: In fast mode this prints `FAST` even when `cargo-clippy` is absent, contradicting the comment that the tooling is present and hiding a missing dependency. Gate the fast branch on the same probe (while retaining the `dry` bypass for `plan`) so a missing tool still reports `SKIP`; apply the same pattern to the review-rule/review-scope branches.
findings.existing_code:
if [ "$fast" -eq 1 ]; then
  fastskip "clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"
elif [ "$dry" -eq 1 ] || command -v cargo-clippy >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  run cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
else
  skip "clippy not installed (rustup component add clippy)"
fi

findings.title: Tighten full-plan assertion for rules check
findings.text: The `check_rules.py` assertion only checks `contains`, so a `FAST … check_rules.py …` or `SKIP … check_rules.py …` line would satisfy it even if the full plan stopped planning the self-check. Require the matched line to start with `PLAN` (the fast plan's `FAST` text names `check_rules.py`), so the test actually guards the full plan.
